_readme: Ratchet for .github/workflows/contracts-coverage.yml. The workflow reads exactly one key —
`lines` — the minimum line coverage over contracts/src that the Sunday cron will accept.
WHY `lines` IS 0 AND `measured` IS null.
Arming this file removes the 'Coverage floor not armed' hard failure, which is the thing that
was stopping the cron from ever completing a run. It does NOT yet constrain anything, because
nothing has measured this tree: `forge coverage --ir-minimum` could not be run at arming time
(forge 1.5.1, solc 0.8.26) — it aborts with a Yul 'too deep in the stack' exception before
emitting lcov.info, with and without script/ excluded, and the non-IR fallback aborts in
script/DeepenLP.s.sol. A floor is a claim about reality; seeding one from a guess would be a
number nobody measured being enforced on everybody, and the first thing it would teach is that
the check lies.
HOW TO ARM IT FOR REAL — one operator action, no code change:
1. Actions -> Contracts Coverage -> Run workflow, with `update_floor` checked.
2. The run prints the measured JSON and does not enforce anything.
3. Commit that number here as `lines`, and set `measured` / `measuredOn` to the same run.
Thereafter the ratchet only moves up: lowering `lines` belongs in the same PR that deliberately
removes the coverage, with the reason in the commit message.
INVARIANT, enforced by frontend/src/test/contractsCoverageFloor.test.ts: `lines` may never
exceed `measured`, and while `measured` is null `lines` must stay 0. A floor above the last
real measurement is a permanently red cron, which is a deleted cron.
If step 1 fails the same way it failed locally, that is the finding: `forge coverage
--ir-minimum` does not work on this contract set at that toolchain, and the workflow needs a
coverage strategy before it needs a floor.
